open_questions: Reconcile Foy’s sabres/bayonets and total including noncombatants with dated returns and the late reinforcement exclusions; establish the intraday Burrard handover.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Source-specific alternatives below retain their own moment and population. Alternatives/limits: Foy says side A had fewer than 10,000 sabres/bayonets on the eve of Vimeiro and about 11,500 at Torres Vedras including noncombatants.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Junot; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Foy gives Delaborde and Loison the infantry divisions, Kellermann the grenadier reserve, Margaron cavalry and Taviel artillery.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable. Alternatives/limits: Oman gives side B 16,778 British troops besides Trant’s 2,000 Portuguese.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Wellesley; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Oman says Burrard arrived offshore and prohibited further offensive movement; Wellesley returned to the army to command the coming battle.
B.army_continuity: Unknown: repeated names and formation labels do not establish continuity.
